steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on unpaired image-to-image translation with Schrödinger bridges (UNSB). Cover why diffusion models with a Gaussian prior are limited for unpaired translation, what existing Schrödinger bridge methods do and why they fail at high resolution, our method, and a bulleted list of contributions.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Diffusion models and their success
2. Limitation: fixed Gaussian prior blocks unpaired translation
3. Schrödinger bridges and deep-learning approaches to them
4. Why no SB method works for unpaired high-resolution translation
5. Diagnosis: curse of dimensionality
6. Our method: UNSB
7. Contributions

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Diffusion models
- generate data by simulating SDEs; remarkable progress in past few years
- diverse and high-quality sample synthesis; hard for GANs, VAEs, flow-based models
- iterative nature useful downstream: image restoration, conditional generation

2. Gaussian prior
- GANs free to choose any prior; diffusion models assume simple prior (Gaussian)
- initial condition for diffusion SDEs fixed to Gaussian noise
- limits unpaired image-to-image translation: domain transfer, style transfer, unpaired image restoration

3. Schrödinger bridges (SBs)
- subset of SDEs; solve entropy-regularized optimal transport (OT); translation between two arbitrary distributions
- deep learning approaches: Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) extended to continuous setting; likelihood training via Forward-Backward SDEs theory; conditional variant of flow matching
- one side simple: two-stage unsupervised procedure, SB between Dirac delta and data
- I2SB, InDI: paired data, SB between Dirac delta and data
- DDIMs as SBs between data and Gaussian -> translation by concatenating two DDIMs (through intermediate Gaussian)

4. Gap
- no work trained SBs for direct high-resolution unpaired translation
- excessive computation, or poor results
- all representative SB methods fail on translating points between two concentric spheres as dimension increases

5. Diagnosis
- main culprit: curse of dimensionality
- higher dimension -> samples sparse, miss shape of image manifold
- sampling error biases SB optimal transport map -> inaccurate SB

6. UNSB
- self-similarity of SB: SB restricted to sub-interval of time domain is also a SB
- SB as sequence of transport cost minimization problems, constraint on KL divergence between true target and model distribution
- Lagrangian formulation -> composition of generators learned via adversarial learning
- mitigates curse of dimensionality on two levels: more advanced discriminator; regularization for inductive bias
- all components scalable -> large scale image translation
- experiments on toy and practical tasks: new research direction for diffusion models in large scale unpaired translation

7. Contributions
- identify curse of dimensionality as cause; toy task as sanity check for OT-based methods
- UNSB: Lagrangian formulation with KL constraint -> composition of adversarially learned generators, advanced discriminators
- improves Denoising Diffusion GAN (arbitrary distributions); generalization of existing unpaired translation methods

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Diffusion models are a class of generative model that generate data by simulating stochastic differential equations (SDEs), and they have made remarkable progress in the past few years. They can synthesize diverse and high-quality samples, which was hard to get for several well-known models like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and flow-based models. Also, the iterative nature of diffusion models turned out to be useful for many downstream tasks, for example image restoration and conditional generation.

But unlike GANs and related models, which can use any prior distribution, diffusion models usually assume a simple prior, like the Gaussian distribution. So the initial condition for diffusion SDEs is generally fixed to be Gaussian noise. Because of this Gaussian assumption, diffusion models can't reach their full potential in unpaired image-to-image translation tasks like domain transfer, style transfer, or unpaired image restoration.

Schrödinger bridges (SBs), which are a subset of SDEs, are a promising solution to this problem. They solve the entropy-regularized optimal transport (OT) problem, and so they allow translation between two arbitrary distributions. Because they are flexible, several approaches have tried to solve SBs with deep learning. For example, one method extends the Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) procedure to the continuous setting, another proposes likelihood training of SBs using Forward-Backward SDEs theory, and a third solves the SB problem with a conditional variant of flow matching.

Some methods solve SBs by assuming that one of the two distributions is simple. One work developed a two-stage unsupervised procedure to estimate the SB between a Dirac delta and data. I2SB and InDI use paired data to learn SBs between a Dirac delta and data. Another work found that DDIMs are SBs between data and Gaussian distributions, so they could do image-to-image translation by concatenating two DDIMs, i.e., by going through an intermediate Gaussian distribution.

4. Gap
- no work so far trained SBs for direct high-resolution unpaired translation
- too much computation, or poor results
- representative SB methods all fail on points between two concentric spheres as dimension increases

5. Diagnosis
- curse of dimensionality is the main culprit
- samples get sparse in high dimension, don't capture the image manifold shape
- sampling error biases the SB optimal transport map -> inaccurate SB

6. UNSB
- self-similarity: SB restricted to a sub-interval of time is also a SB
- sequence of transport cost minimization problems with KL constraint (true target vs model distribution)
- Lagrangian formulation = composition of generators from adversarial learning
- two levels against curse of dimensionality: better discriminator, regularization for inductive bias
- scalable components -> large scale image translation
- toy and practical experiments -> new research direction

7. Contributions
- curse of dimensionality identified as cause; toy sanity check
- UNSB with Lagrangian formulation and KL constraint; advanced discriminators
- improves Denoising Diffusion GAN; generalizes existing unpaired translation methods

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Diffusion models are a class of generative model that generate data by simulating stochastic differential equations (SDEs), and they have made remarkable progress in the past few years. They can synthesize diverse and high-quality samples, which was hard to get for several well-known models like Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), and flow-based models. Also, the iterative nature of diffusion models turned out to be useful for many downstream tasks, for example image restoration and conditional generation.

But unlike GANs and related models, which can use any prior distribution, diffusion models usually assume a simple prior, like the Gaussian distribution. So the initial condition for diffusion SDEs is generally fixed to be Gaussian noise. Because of this Gaussian assumption, diffusion models can't reach their full potential in unpaired image-to-image translation tasks like domain transfer, style transfer, or unpaired image restoration.

Schrödinger bridges (SBs), which are a subset of SDEs, are a promising solution to this problem. They solve the entropy-regularized optimal transport (OT) problem, and so they allow translation between two arbitrary distributions. Because they are flexible, several approaches have tried to solve SBs with deep learning. For example, one method extends the Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) procedure to the continuous setting, another proposes likelihood training of SBs using Forward-Backward SDEs theory, and a third solves the SB problem with a conditional variant of flow matching.

Some methods solve SBs by assuming that one of the two distributions is simple. One work developed a two-stage unsupervised procedure to estimate the SB between a Dirac delta and data. I2SB and InDI use paired data to learn SBs between a Dirac delta and data. Another work found that DDIMs are SBs between data and Gaussian distributions, so they could do image-to-image translation by concatenating two DDIMs, i.e., by going through an intermediate Gaussian distribution.

However, as far as we know, no work so far has successfully trained SBs for direct translation between high-resolution images in the unpaired setting. Most methods need too much computation, and even when they don't, we see poor results. In fact, all representative SB methods fail even on the simple task of translating points between two concentric spheres when the dimension increases.

In this work, we first identify the curse of dimensionality as the main reason why SB fails for unpaired image-to-image translation. When the dimension of the data increases, the samples become more and more sparse and fail to capture the shape of the underlying image manifold. This sampling error then biases the SB optimal transport map, and this leads to an inaccurate SB.

We use the self-similarity of SB, which is the interesting property that SB restricted to a sub-interval of its time domain is also a SB. Based on this we propose the Unpaired Neural Schrödinger Bridge (UNSB), which formulates the SB problem as a sequence of transport cost minimization problems with a constraint on the KL divergence between the true target distribution and the model distribution. We show that its Lagrangian formulation naturally expresses the SB as a composition of generators learned via adversarial learning. An important advantage of the UNSB formulation is that it lets us mitigate the curse of dimensionality on two levels: we can extend the discriminator in adversarial learning to a more advanced one, and we can add regularization so that the generator learns a mapping that aligns with our inductive bias. Also, all components of UNSB are scalable, so UNSB naturally scales to large scale image translation problems too.

Experiments on toy and practical image-to-image translation tasks show that UNSB opens up a new research direction for using diffusion models on large scale unpaired translation tasks. Our contributions are the following.

- We identify the curse of dimensionality as the cause of the failure of previous SB methods for image-to-image translation. We verify this empirically with a toy task used as a sanity check for whether an OT-based method is robust to the curse of dimensionality.

- We propose UNSB, which formulates SB as a Lagrangian formulation with a constraint on the KL divergence between the true target distribution and the model distribution. This gives a composition of generators learned via adversarial learning that overcome the curse of dimensionality with advanced discriminators.

- UNSB improves on the Denoising Diffusion GAN by allowing translation between arbitrary distributions. Also, by comparing with other existing unpaired translation methods, we show that UNSB is really a generalization of them that overcomes their shortcomings.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Diffusion models [1,2,3,4], a class of generative model which generates data by simulating stochastic differential equations (SDEs), have achieved remarkable progress over the past few years. They are capable of diverse and high-quality sample synthesis [5], a desideratum that was difficult to obtain for several widely acknowledged models such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) [6], Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) [7], and flow-based models [8]. Furthermore, the iterative nature of diffusion models has proved useful for a variety of downstream tasks, e.g., image restoration [9] and conditional generation [10].

However, unlike GANs and their family, which are free to choose any prior distribution, diffusion models often assume a simple prior such as the Gaussian distribution. In other words, the initial condition for diffusion SDEs is generally fixed to be Gaussian noise. This Gaussian assumption prevents diffusion models from unlocking their full potential in unpaired image-to-image translation tasks such as domain transfer, style transfer, or unpaired image restoration.

Schrödinger bridges (SBs), a subset of SDEs, present a promising solution to this issue. They solve the entropy-regularized optimal transport (OT) problem, enabling translation between two arbitrary distributions. Their flexibility has motivated several approaches to solving SBs via deep learning. For instance, [11] extends the Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) procedure to the continuous setting, [12] proposes likelihood training of SBs using Forward-Backward SDEs theory, and [13] solves the SB problem with a conditional variant of flow matching.

Some methods have solved SBs assuming that one of the two distributions is simple. [14] developed a two-stage unsupervised procedure for estimating the SB between a Dirac delta and data. I2SB [15] and InDI [16] use paired data to learn SBs between a Dirac delta and data. [17] discovered DDIMs [3] as SBs between data and Gaussian distributions, and were thus able to perform image-to-image translation by concatenating two DDIMs, i.e., by passing through an intermediate Gaussian distribution.

Yet, to the best of our knowledge, no work so far has successfully trained SBs for direct translation between high-resolution images in the unpaired setting. Most methods demand excessive computation, and even when they do not, we observe poor results. In fact, all representative SB methods fail even on the simple task of translating points between two concentric spheres as the dimension increases.

In this work, we first identify the curse of dimensionality as the main culprit behind the failure of SB for unpaired image-to-image translation. As the dimension of the data increases, the samples become increasingly sparse and fail to capture the shape of the underlying image manifold. This sampling error then biases the SB optimal transport map, leading to an inaccurate SB.

Based on the self-similarity of SB, the intriguing property that SB restricted to a sub-interval of its time domain is also a SB, we propose the Unpaired Neural Schrödinger Bridge (UNSB), which formulates the SB problem as a sequence of transport cost minimization problems under a constraint on the KL divergence between the true target distribution and the model distribution. We show that its Lagrangian formulation naturally expresses the SB as a composition of generators learned via adversarial learning [6]. An important advantage of the UNSB formulation is that it allows us to mitigate the curse of dimensionality on two levels: we can extend the discriminator in adversarial learning to a more advanced one, and we can add regularization to enforce that the generator learns a mapping aligned with our inductive bias. Furthermore, since all components of UNSB are scalable, UNSB naturally scales to large scale image translation problems as well.

Experiments on toy and practical image-to-image translation tasks demonstrate that UNSB opens up a new research direction for applying diffusion models to large scale unpaired translation tasks. Our contributions can be summarized as follows.

- • We identify the curse of dimensionality as the cause behind the failure of previous SB methods for image-to-image translation, and verify this empirically using a toy task as a sanity check for whether an OT-based method is robust to the curse of dimensionality.

- • We propose UNSB, which formulates SB as a Lagrangian formulation under a constraint on the KL divergence between the true target distribution and the model distribution. This leads to a composition of generators learned via adversarial learning that overcome the curse of dimensionality with advanced discriminators.

- • UNSB improves upon the Denoising Diffusion GAN [5] by enabling translation between arbitrary distributions. Furthermore, through comparison with other existing unpaired translation methods, we demonstrate that UNSB is indeed a generalization of them that overcomes their shortcomings.
